decisions.why: The psalm opens and closes on the same words (the Latin's frame), so one slot fills both. The soul is a single addressee → *tu* (rule 3). The glossary row *benedícere* (man → God) keeps the dative → *bendizei ao Senhor*; Ps 95:2 moved a dative to the direct object because *ao seu nome* blurred into *ao Senhor* — that reason is absent here. The vocative without *ó*, as the settled refrain 41:6 *Por que estás triste, minha alma?*. The same line opens Ps 102 (102:1, 102:2, 102:22), translated in parallel by another agent: **the coordinator should make the two psalms agree**. **Finish:** Ps 102 set the formula row *Bendize, ó minha alma, ao Senhor* (dative kept, with *ó*); 103:1 and 103:35 copy it.

decisions.why: ἐμεγαλύνθης σφόδρα: a passive whose sense is 'you have become great'. The formula 91:6 = 103:24 *Quam magnificáta sunt ópera tua* is already *Como se engrandeceram*, the reflexive; the same verb in the same psalm should read the same, so the reflexive here too (MS1932 *tu te engrandeceste sumamente*). The enclisis *engrandecestes-vos* answers *Vestistes-vos* at the head of 1b. *veheménter → muito* (row *valde / veheménter*, as 20:2 *exultará muito*). **v2:** the Latinist asked the passive and the ambiguity reader heard *engrandecer-se* as possibly self-aggrandizement, said of God; taken. 103:24 keeps the 91:6 formula (the works, where the reflexive cannot mislead); the root still links the two verses.

options.note: proclisis; *grandemente* the row's local option for *veheménter*

decisions.why: The twin of 95:6 *Conféssio, et pulchritúdo*, which ruled *Confissão* (the Latin's word, keeping the praise confessed and, for some readers, the sin confessed) and asked that 103:1 decide with it. Decided with it: the same noun. *decor → esplendor* (row; 92:1a *vestiu-se de esplendor*), kept apart from 95:6 *pulchritúdo → beleza*, as the *decor* row wants, so a reader hears two twins with one different word, as in the Latin. *induísti* (active, ἐνεδύσω middle) → *Vestistes-vos de*, the verb of 92:1a. Cost, as at 95:6: *confissão* is heard first as the sacrament. The Latin puts the objects first; Portuguese order puts the verb first (D2).

decisions.latin: amíctus lúmine sicut vestiménto … sicut vestiméntum, amíctus ejus
decisions.why: The Latin uses *amíctus* twice, first as a participle (God 'wrapped' in light), then as a noun (the abyss is 'its cloak'), each time beside *sicut vestiméntum*. Portuguese has no participle and noun of one root that both sound natural (*envolto / envoltório*). *vestiméntum → veste* is kept in both verses, so the pairing is still heard; *amíctus* becomes *envolto* and *manto*. In 103:6 *ejus* is the earth's or God's (Latin and Greek leave it open; MS1932 decides *cinge-a*, the earth): *o seu manto* keeps both.

options.label: coberto … o seu manto
options.note: MS1932 *coberto de luz*; but *cobrir* is *tégere*'s in 103:2

options.label: envolto … o que o envolve
options.note: one root twice, as the Latin; but the pronoun must take a gender and so decides whose cloak it is

decisions.why: *pellis* is a hide (δέρριν), the stuff tents were made of (L&S: *sub pellibus* 'in camp'). The concrete image stays (rule 5): the sky stretched out like a skin. DRB 'pavilion' and MS1932 *pavilhão* explain it as the tent; that is the image behind it, not the word.

options.label: uma tenda de peles
options.note: keeps the skin and says what it is for; adds the tent

decisions.why: The same Latin noun twice (τὰ ὑπερῷα, 'upper rooms'), so one Portuguese phrase twice. *alturas* is taken by *excélsa* (D42). *partes altas* is the plain sense of the neuter plural and MS1932's (*a sua parte superior*); DRB keeps the Greek's rooms. In 103:13 *suis* is God's, though he is addressed as *vós* two words later (*óperum tuórum*): the Latin's shift of person is kept.

*ascénsus* is an ascent, or (L&S, by metonymy) 'a place by which one ascends'; ἐπίβασις the same. God sets the cloud as his way up. DRB 'chariot' is the Hebrew's picture. *pôr … como* for the double accusative. **v2:** *pôr … por* (stylist; the ambiguity reader also heard *como* as a simile).

options.label: por vossa subida
options.note: v2 — the stylist: *pôr por* = set as (as *ter por*, *tomar por*); *como* was heard as a comparison

options.label: como vosso degrau
options.note: the concrete 'place by which one ascends'

decisions.why: *spíritus* (πνεύματα) is 'spirits' and 'winds'; after 103:3's winds the verse can mean either, and Heb 1:7 quotes it for the angels' nature. *espíritos* keeps the Latin's word and the reading the Church kept; *ventos* is MS1932's gloss. *fazer de X Y* is how Portuguese says the double accusative.

options.label: ventos
options.note: MS1932's gloss; closes the ambiguity the other way

decisions.why: *stabílitas* (ἀσφάλεια) is firmness, steadiness. *estabilidade* is the cognate and plain; *firmeza* is shorter but 96:2 has just given it to *corréctio*; MS1932 and DRB say 'bases', which is the Hebrew's word. **v2:** *firmeza* (stylist; +4 syllables in v1). It meets 96:2 *corréctio → firmeza* (an open row) in another psalm; noted for the glossary.

options.label: a sua firmeza
options.note: v2 — the stylist: plainer, and the colon loses two syllables; the 96:2 *corréctio* row is open and far away

decisions.why: *stare* → *estar de pé* (open row), but waters 'standing up' is odd; the row's other form, *deter-se* (1:1 *non stetit*), says that the waters stand still over the mountains — and in 103:7 they flee. MS1932 *elevam-se* interprets.

The row *formidáre (a) → ter pavor de* names this verse as the same build as 118:161. Kept apart from *timére → temer*. *À vossa repreensão* is the formula of 17:16b and 75:7; the second *a* is given the same crasis (*à voz*), as 41:8 *à voz das vossas cataratas*.

*emíttere* is the verb of 103:30 *Emíttes spíritum tuum* (both ἐξαποστέλλω): the psalm sends forth springs and then the spirit. The repetition is kept with *enviar* in both. *Enviar fontes* is less usual than *fazer brotar*, which would say the image more easily and lose the echo. *pelos vales* rather than *nos vales*: with *enviar* the place needs a preposition of movement. **v2:** *nos vales* (Latinist).

options.label: enviais as fontes nos vales
options.note: v2 — the Latinist: *in convállibus* is *nos vales*; *pelos* borrowed 10b's movement

decisions.latin: béstiæ agri · juméntis · béstiæ silvæ (and 103:26 animália)
decisions.why: Three Latin words for animals stand in the psalm: *béstiæ* (θηρία, wild beasts, 103:11, 20), *juménta* (κτήνη, beasts kept by man, 103:14), *animália* (ζῷα, 103:26). The *juménta* row gives *animais*, but here *animália* needs that word, and the Greek keeps all three apart. So: *béstiæ → feras* (49:10 *feræ silvárum → as feras das selvas* is the same Greek, θηρία τοῦ δρυμοῦ, so they share it), *juménta → o gado* (the row's own option), *animália → animais*.

options.label: feras · os animais
options.note: the *juménta* row; *animais* then serves two Latin words in one psalm

decisions.why: *exhilaráre* (ἱλαρῦναι) is a different verb from *lætificáre* (εὐφραίνει) one colon earlier; *alegrar* is already *lætificáre*'s. *animar* is the Brazilian verb for cheering someone up and keeps them apart. Who does it is left open, as in the Latin (third person, no subject: the man, the oil, God). *óleo*, as 22:5, 44:8, 54:22.

options.label: torne alegre
options.note: the sense exactly; shares the root of *alegre* in 103:14b

decisions.why: The *confirmáre* row: with a person or a heart as object *confirmar* is heard as attesting; the row proposes *firmar* for persons, and 36:17 took *sustentar* (ὑποστηρίζει; here στηρίζει). Bread sustains, so *sustentar* is the sense and the verb 36:17 already gave. *firme o coração* would be the row's proposal; MS1932 *fortifique*. **v2:** *fortaleça* (Latinist: στηρίζει, make firm; *sustente* feeds rather than strengthens). Avoids *confirmar* as the row asks; the 26:14 formula already uses *fortalecer-se* for *confortári*, a different Latin verb, in another psalm.

options.label: fortaleça
options.note: v2 — the Latinist: *confirmáre* is to make strong; *sustentar* softened it. MS1932, DRB

decisions.why: A hard line in the Latin too. *heródius* is the Greek ἐρωδιός, the heron; L&S: 'an unknown bird, perhaps the stork'; MS1932 *cegonha* (the Hebrew's bird). The Latin says 'the heron's house is their leader' (ἡ οἰκία ἡγεῖται αὐτῶν); DRB turns it into 'the highest of them is the house of the heron'. Kept as the Latin says it, without explaining. *dux → guia* (open row).

decisions.why: *cognóvit* is a perfect with present sense (ἔγνω, gnomic; DRB 'knoweth'), like *cognóvi → conheço* (D44); *conheceu* would be heard as a single event, even the sun's death. *occásus → poente*, as the settled formula 49:1 *até o poente*.

The *collocáre* row gives *colocar* (22:1 *ali me colocou*). Here the passive is 'they will be laid down' in their dens (κοιτασθήσονται, 'will lie down'; L&S *collocare in cubili*). *serão colocados nos seus covis* is not how Portuguese says an animal lying down. *se deitarão* is the sense of the Latin word in this use.

*posséssio* (κτῆσις, what one has acquired). The row *heréditas / posséssio* keeps *posse* for land; 77:48 took *bens* where the goods were meant, because *posse* is heard as the right of owning. Here too the earth is full of what God owns. DRB 'riches', MS1932 *riquezas*.

decisions.latin: Hoc mare magnum, et spatiósum mánibus
decisions.why: 'Wide of hands' (εὐρύχωρος; the Hebrew's idiom). Portuguese cannot say a sea is wide of hands, but it says *braços de mar*, and MS1932 *de longos braços*: the limb is kept, only its name changes. The verse is verbless in the Latin and stays so.

options.label: espaçoso de mãos
options.note: the Latin word for word; not Portuguese

decisions.latin: illic reptília, quorum non est númerus
decisions.why: The *reptília* row gives *tudo o que rasteja* (68:35, where the Latin has *ómnia*); here there is no *ómnia*. *répteis* is zoological. The neuter plural becomes a verb with a supplied noun (grammar, D2); *quorum non est númerus* → *sem número*, the same compression 104:34 and 146:5 will face.

options.label: ali, o que rasteja, que não tem número

forms.reptilia: ali, o que rasteja, que não tem número

decisions.latin: Draco iste, quem formásti ad illudéndum ei
decisions.why: *illúdere* + dative: 'to play with' or 'to make sport of, mock' (L&S). *ei* can be the sea (DRB 'to play therein', MS1932 *brincar entre as suas ondas*) or the dragon (God made him to make sport of him; ἐμπαίζειν αὐτῷ). *brincar com ele* keeps both: *ele* is *o mar* or *o dragão*. *zombar dele* decides for the mockery and the dragon; *illúsio → escárnio* (D39) is that sense's word elsewhere.

options.label: para zombar dele
options.note: the mocking sense; decides the pronoun

decisions.latin: ómnia in sapiéntia fecísti · ómnia a te exspéctant · ómnia implebúntur
decisions.why: Three times *ómnia*, neuter plural. In 103:24 it is 'all things' (*tudo*). In 103:27–28 the neuter is the creatures who wait and are fed (*illis*); *todas as coisas aguardam … que lhes deis o alimento* makes 'things' eat. MS1932 has *todos* there. The repetition is kept between 27 and 28; 24 differs by one word's grammar.

D16 and D26 make *elóquium* the clause *o que dissestes* when it is God's word; D16 names 103:34, a man's word, as a place the verse decides. The clause works here as a subject, in the present because the psalmist's speech is the psalm now being said (διαλογή, his discourse): *o que eu digo*. It stays apart from *palavra* (*verbum*, *sermo*). *jucúndus → agradável* (row). **v2:** the Latinist and the stylist both asked *a minha palavra*; refused — *palavra* already carries *verbum* and *sermo* (glossary row), and D16/D26 keep *elóquium* apart. The stylist's cadence point taken by dropping *eu*: *o que DI-go*, and the emphatic *eu, porém* of 34b now answers it alone.

options.label: o que digo
options.note: v2 — D26's clause without *eu*, which the stylist found weak at the mediant; *eu* now stands only in 34b (*ego vero*)

options.label: a minha palavra
options.note: Latinist and stylist, v1; merges with *verbum / sermo*

decisions.why: *defícere → desfalecer* (row) stands in 103:29 (*e desfalecerão*); but *desfalecer da terra* is not Portuguese. ἐκλίποισαν: 'fail, vanish'. *Desapareçam da terra* (MS1932) says it; the echo with 103:29 is lost.

options.label: Desfaleçam da terra
options.note: the row's verb and 103:29's; not idiomatic with *da terra*

choices.103:1: The frame of the psalm (103:1a = 103:35b) fills both places from one decision. *Dómine, Deus meus → Senhor, meu Deus* (formula row). The soul is *tu*, God is *vós*, both in one verse as the Latin has it. Checks: The remaining ±3–4 flags (103:1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, 14, 14b, 15, 21, 22, 23, 24, 28, 30, 32) come from Portuguese articles and analytic verbs; none moves a cadence off oxytone/paroxytone.
choices.103:2: The participles of 103:1b–2 (*amíctus … Exténdens*) and the relatives *qui* (103:2b–5, 103:10) hang on *Dómine* of 103:1 without a main verb; kept so. *Qui* → *vós que* each time: the anaphora is the Latin's. *tégere → cobrir* (row); 103:9 *operíre* also becomes *cobrir* (a different Greek verb: στεγάζω / καλύπτω) — they do not meet in one verse.
choices.103:5: *inclináre* → *inclinar-se* (settled row, of kingdoms); DRB 'moved'. *in sǽculum sǽculi → pelos séculos dos séculos* (D27).
choices.103:7: *Ab increpatióne tua → À vossa repreensão*, the formula of 17:16b and 75:7. *tonítruum → trovão* (row *in rota*).
choices.103:8: The Latin's ':' after *montes* and the mediant after *campi* are both kept. *campi → campos*, as 95:11 *campi gaudébunt → os campos*; *ager* (103:11) also becomes *campo*, so two Latin words (πεδίον, ἀγρός) share one Portuguese — they are eight verses apart. *fundásti* repeats 103:5's *fundastes*.
choices.103:10: *pertransíre → passar* (38:7), kept one verb in all three places of the psalm (103:10, 20, 26).
choices.103:11: *Potábunt* — in Vulgate Latin *potáre* can mean 'give to drink' (the Greek ποτιοῦσιν does), but *béstiæ* is nominative, so in the Latin the beasts drink. *ónager → asnos selvagens* (*jumento* is a donkey in Brazil, *onagro* unknown). *exspectáre → aguardar* (D39).
choices.103:12: *Super ea* is neuter in the Latin (Greek αὐτά, the waters, ὕδατα neuter); *Sobre elas* refers the ear to *as águas* of 103:10b. *vocem dare → fazer ouvir a voz* (row; 17:14); the plural kept; no possessive, as the Latin (*dabunt voces*; v2 gate). *petra → rocha* (row). **v2 (ambiguity reader):** *Sobre elas* may be heard with *feras* (103:11); the Latin *ea* is equally a bare pronoun (the waters of 103:10). Kept, not glossed.
choices.103:13: *rigáre → regar* (row). *satiáre / saturáre → saciar* (row; one Greek verb, χορτάζω, in 103:13 and 103:16), passive as in the Latin. **v2:** *se saciará* (stylist: the analytic passive was heavy); the Latin passive is medio-passive (D2). 103:16 takes the same form, so one Greek verb (χορτάζω) keeps one shape.
choices.103:14: *fænum → feno* here (fodder for the herd; the row's split: *erva* where it flowers), *herba → erva* (row), so the two words stay apart in one verse. *servitúti hóminum* kept as *o serviço dos homens* (DRB 'the service of men').
choices.103:14b: *edúcere → fazer sair* (row). The subjunctive of the second colon is announced with *que* (*e que o vinho alegre*), because *e o vinho alegre …* is first heard as 'the cheerful wine'. *lætificáre → alegrar* (row). 103:15 repeats the build.
choices.103:15: Checks: the rhyme 103:14b/103:15 (*homem*) is the Latin's own repetition (*cor hóminis* twice); kept. v2 checks: 15b +5 with *fortaleça* (the Latinist's verb); accepted.
choices.103:16: *que ele plantou*: the Latin's third person (God), inside a psalm that addresses him. *cedri* is feminine in Latin, *cedros* masculine; nothing hangs on it. *passer → pardal* (row, which names this verse). *nidificáre → fazer ninho*. **v2:** *As árvores do campo se saciarão* — the stylist asked a pronominal (his *Saciam-se* changes the tense; refused); the subject is put first to avoid a proclitic at the head of the verse. Checks: +6 (the Portuguese articles and the supplied *ele*); accepted.
choices.103:17: *excélsus → excelso* (D43). *cervus → cervo* kept: the row allows it where the animal's context is clear, as here between the heron and the hedgehog. *herinácius* (hedgehog; χοιρογρύλλιος, the rock-badger) → *ouriços*, MS1932. The second half is verbless in the Latin; one copula is supplied (*são*), the second clause keeps the Latin's ellipsis. Checks: +6 — the supplied *são* and prepositions; accepted. **v2 (ambiguity reader):** *ouriços* may be heard as sea urchins; *ouriço* is also the land animal (MS1932), and *porco-espinho* is another animal. Kept.
choices.103:20: *Posuísti* repeats 103:9 *Pusestes*. *silva → selva* (D44), though readers have objected to it in three psalms; left for the coordinator.
choices.103:21: The verse has no main verb in the Latin: the lion cubs are in apposition to the beasts of 103:20b. The gerund keeps that. *cátulus → filhote* (row; 16:12 *um filhote de leão*); *rugíre → rugir*; *rápere → arrebatar* (row); *quǽrere → buscar* (row); *esca → alimento* (the row foresees *alimento* or *comida* for food given; 103:27 has the same word, and *alimento* serves both).
choices.103:22: *oríri → nascer* (row); *congregári → reunir-se* (D43); the subject pronoun *eles* supplied (D2), otherwise the sun seems to gather. *cubíle → covil*.
choices.103:23: *opus → obra* (as 103:13, 24, 31); *operátio → trabalho* (a different noun of the same root; *operação* is not said of a man's labour). *usque ad vésperum → até a tarde* (58:7 *à tarde*).
choices.103:24: The formula of 91:6a: *Como se engrandeceram as vossas obras, Senhor!* *implére → encher*, in 103:24 and 103:28 alike. *in sapiéntia → com sabedoria*.
choices.103:27: *formáre → formar* (94:5). *in témpore → a seu tempo*, the Portuguese idiom for 'in due time' (Greek εὔκαιρον).
choices.103:28: The two absolute ablatives stay gerunds, each with its subject *vós* (MS1932's build). *bónitas → bondade* (row). *aperíre* is not an imperative here, so rule 3 does not apply.
choices.103:29: *avértere fáciem → desviar a face* (row, 12:1); the Latin has no *tuam* and the Portuguese none. *turbári → perturbar-se* (row). *auferre → tirar* (D41). *spíritum eórum … spíritum tuum* (103:30): *espírito* both times, so the play between their spirit taken and yours sent is heard; lower case, as the DO Latin and 50:13 (D44). *defícere → desfalecer* (row); *revérti → voltar*; *pulvis → pó*.
choices.103:30: Lower case *espírito*, as the DO Latin prints *spíritum*. The Pentecost versicle's words (*Emítte Spíritum tuum*) are an imperative in the liturgy, a future here; the psalm's future is kept.
choices.103:31: *Sit … in sǽculum → Seja … para sempre* (D23). *lætári → alegrar-se* (row).
choices.103:32: *respícere → olhar para* (row). *Ele, que* opens the verse: the Latin's *Qui* hangs on *Dóminus* of 103:31b, and a verse cannot open on a bare *Que*. *eles fumegam*: the subject supplied (D2).
choices.103:33: *Cantábo … psallam*: *cantar* and *entoar salmos* side by side, as 12:6b (D25). *in vita mea → na minha vida* (62:5). *quámdiu sum → enquanto eu existir* (*esse* absolute → *existir*, D39). Checks: +8 syllables — *psallam → entoarei salmos* (D25) and *sum → eu existir* (D39) each cost a word; accepted for the formulas.
choices.103:35: *ita ut non sint → de modo que já não existam* (*esse* absolute → *existir*, D39; *já* as 38:14 *e já não existirei*). *peccátor / iníquus → pecador / iníquo* (row). Checks: the rhyme 103:34/103:35 (*Senhor*) — the Latin ends both on *Dómino*; kept. **v2:** *ita ut non sint → até não existirem mais* (stylist: *de modo que* was the register of an explanation); *até* keeps the result, *não … mais* the *já* of 38:14. v2 checks: +6; accepted.

D44 (settled): *cognóvi* with present sense → *conheço*; the perfect would be heard as a single past event.
The formula of 91:6a (*Como se engrandeceram*), kept word for word; 103:1 took the passive (v2).
*possessão* is heard first as demonic possession in Brazil; *bens* as 77:48; *posse* option 1.
*espaçoso de mãos* is not Portuguese (option 1); *braços de mar* keeps a limb. *répteis* is zoological (option 2).
*todas as coisas aguardam … que lhes deis o alimento* makes things eat; option 1 keeps the neuter.
